result.title: Householder Motion Embedding: Noise Modulation for Motion-Controllable Video Generation
result.summary: Diffusion models for video generation have achieved remarkable success, yet precise motion control under explicit user guidance remains challenging. Recent noise-warping methods introduce temporal correlations by warping the noise according to the user-provided motion signal. However, standard spatial warping generally disrupts the noise's i.i.d. Gaussian structure, requiring distribution correction, such as Jacobian-based correction, but at a substantial computational overhead. We propose Householder Motion Embedding (HME), which encodes the motion signal into the noise through a sequence of Householder reflections that together form an orthogonal transformation applied to each location's channel vector. HME exactly preserves the spatial Gaussian structure within each frame while introducing cross-frame correlations that promote temporally consistent video. HME is agnostic to the network architecture and integrates directly into standard video diffusion fine-tuning pipelines. Experiments on different scenarios show that HME matches or outperforms the state of the art, while achieving a 2.7x speedup over noise warping. These results demonstrate that channel-space Householder transformations offer a principled and efficient alternative to noise warping for motion-controllable video generation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Householder Motion Embedding，用一串 Householder 反射构成的正交变换把运动信号嵌入每帧噪声的通道向量，在保持帧内高斯结构的同时引入跨帧相关性，用于运动可控视频生成。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于视频扩散生成中的噪声调控与运动控制，不涉及视觉推理状态、证据获取或停止决策；正交保结构变换虽与 latent 更新有形式相似，但材料未提供可核查的 LVR 借鉴线索。
